chunks.title: Commissioning service
chunks.text:
Our engineers can commission systems with more than 3 fans or any air handling unit: airflow measurement, balancing, controller setup and a protocol for the customer.

Price: $350 per day plus travel outside the city. Book at least 5 business days ahead through a task to the service department.

chunks.title: How to create a quote in the CRM
chunks.text: 1. Open the customer card and press "New quote". If the customer is new, create the customer first: a quote cannot exist without one. 2. Add items from the catalogue by model code (for example NW-ID-200) or with the selection wizard. The price and availability come from the catalogue and cannot be typed by hand. 3. Set the discount. Anything above 5% sends an approval request automatically (see the discount approval matrix). 4. Choose delivery: pickup, courier or pallet. Free delivery is applied automatically above $1,500. 5. Press "Send to customer". The CRM generates a PDF with the validity period (14 days by default) and logs the e-mail on the customer timeline.

A quote does not reserve stock. To hold items for a customer, convert the quote into an order or create a reservation (see "Stock reservations").

chunks.title: Logging customer calls
chunks.text:
After every call with a customer, add a note to the customer timeline: what was discussed, what was promised and the next step with a date. Calls through the office phone are attached automatically; you only add the note and the next step.

A next step without a date is not a next step: the CRM will not remind you about it.

chunks.title: Discount approval matrix
chunks.text:
Sales managers may give up to 5% off the list price on their own.

From 5% to 12% the discount needs the approval of the head of sales: create an approval request from the quote ("Request discount") and explain the reason (competitor offer, volume, strategic customer).

Above 12% only the sales director can approve, and only for project deals with a signed specification.

Discounts never stack with the volume price list. Spare parts and commissioning services are not discounted.

chunks.title: EC vs AC motors
chunks.text:
EC (electronically commutated) motors are 25-40% more efficient than AC motors, have built-in speed control (0-10 V or Modbus) and run quieter at partial speed. They cost 30-60% more.

AC motors need an external speed controller or a frequency converter for speed control. They are simpler to repair and cheaper to buy.

Recommend EC when the fan runs more than 8 hours a day, when speed control is needed, or when noise matters. For short daily operation AC is usually the better buy.

chunks.title: Fan selection basics: airflow, pressure, duty point
chunks.text:
A fan is chosen for a duty point: the airflow the system needs (m³/h) and the static pressure the fan has to overcome at that airflow (Pa).

The pressure comes from the ductwork: duct length, bends, grilles, filters and silencers. A short duct with a grille needs 50-150 Pa; a supply system with a filter and a heater easily needs 300-500 Pa.

Read the fan curve at the required airflow. The fan fits if its pressure at that airflow is at least the required pressure. Keep a margin of 10-20%: filters load up with dust and the pressure grows over time. A much larger margin means a noisier, more expensive fan that runs throttled.

If the customer only knows the room size, use air changes: an office needs about 3-4 air changes per hour, a kitchen 10-15, a warehouse 1-2. Airflow = room volume × air changes.

chunks.title: Filter classes and maintenance
chunks.text:
G4 (coarse) filters protect equipment from dust and insects. F7 / ePM1 60% filters are needed for offices and anything with people in it.

Replace filters when the pressure drop doubles compared to a clean filter, or at least every 3-6 months. A clogged filter is the most common cause of "low airflow" claims.

Spare filters are sold by model: the code is FL-<unit code>-<class>, for example FL-NW-ID-200-F7.

chunks.title: Installation checklist for inline duct fans
chunks.text: 1. Install with the airflow arrow in the direction of flow. 2. Leave at least 1 duct diameter of straight duct before and 1.5 after the fan. 3. Use flexible connectors on both sides to stop vibration travelling along the duct. 4. Fit a motor protection device; without it the warranty is void. 5. Keep access for service: the cover must open without removing the fan. 6. Check the current draw after start-up; it must not exceed the nameplate value.

chunks.title: Invoice corrections and credit notes
chunks.text:
Never edit a sent invoice. If the amount, the items or the customer details are wrong, issue a credit note for the full invoice and a new corrected invoice.

In the CRM: open the invoice, press "Credit note", choose "Full" or "Partial" and the reason. Finance approves credit notes above $1,000.

chunks.title: IT requests: passwords, hardware, access
chunks.text:
Create a task for the IT department from the CRM (Tasks → New task → IT). Password resets are done within 1 hour during working time; new hardware within 3 business days.

Never send passwords by e-mail or chat.

chunks.title: Kitchen exhaust requirements
chunks.text:
Commercial kitchen exhaust needs fans rated for at least 120 °C continuous air temperature and a grease filter in the hood.

Only roof fans of the NW-RF series (rated for 120 °C) are approved for kitchen exhaust. Axial wall fans and inline duct fans are not suitable.

Airflow for a kitchen hood: about 1,000-1,500 m³/h per metre of hood length.

chunks.title: Lead qualification checklist
chunks.text:
Before quoting a new lead, find out: - the object type and rooms (office, restaurant, warehouse, flat); - the airflow or the room sizes, and what is installed now; - who decides and who pays (contractor, end customer, designer); - the deadline and the budget; - whether a project specification exists.

Log the answers in the lead card. A lead without object type and deadline is not passed to a quote.

chunks.title: Model codes
chunks.text: NW-AX — axial wall fans, the number is the impeller diameter in mm (NW-AX-400). NW-ID — circular inline duct fans, the number is the duct diameter (NW-ID-200 fits a 200 mm duct). NW-RD — rectangular duct fans, the numbers are the duct size in cm (NW-RD-60-30). NW-RF — roof fans. The suffix E means an EC motor (NW-ID-200E). All NW-RF roof fans are rated for 120 °C air.

chunks.title: Noise levels: what is acceptable where
chunks.text:
Catalogue noise values are sound pressure levels in dB(A) at 3 m in free field.

Typical limits: bedrooms and hotel rooms 30-35 dB(A), offices and meeting rooms 35-40, restaurants and shops 45-50, workshops 60-70.

Every 10 dB(A) sounds twice as loud. EC fans at reduced speed are 5-8 dB(A) quieter than at full speed, which is why oversized EC fans running slowly can be a good choice for quiet rooms.

Duct silencers reduce noise by 10-25 dB(A) and add 20-50 Pa of pressure loss; include that in the duty point.

chunks.title: First week for new sales managers
chunks.text: Day 1: accounts, CRM access, phone. Read the discount, payment and returns policies. Day 2: product training — model codes, fan selection basics, EC vs AC. Day 3: shadow a senior manager on calls. Day 4: create test quotes in the CRM training space. Day 5: first own leads, with a senior manager reviewing every quote for two weeks.

chunks.title: Payment terms and credit limits
chunks.text:
New customers pay 100% in advance for the first three orders.

After three paid orders a customer can get net-30 terms with a credit limit set by the finance department (usually $5,000-$20,000). The limit and the current balance are on the customer card, visible to sales only.

When an invoice is more than 30 days overdue, the customer goes on credit hold: new orders need prepayment until the debt is paid. Sales managers get a daily list of overdue invoices in their briefing.

chunks.title: Returns and warranty policy
chunks.text:
All fans and air handling units sold by Northwind Air carry a 24-month manufacturer warranty from the date of delivery. Filters, belts and other consumables are not covered.

Stock items can be returned within 14 days of delivery if they are unused and in the original packaging. A 15% restocking fee applies; the fee is waived when the return is caused by our error (wrong model shipped, damaged in transit).

Made-to-order units (anything with the status "on order" at the time of the sale, custom voltages, special coatings) cannot be returned. Warranty still applies to them.

A warranty claim is accepted only with the serial number, the invoice number and photos of the nameplate and of the fault. Units that were installed without a motor protection device or outside the allowed air temperature range lose their warranty.

Refunds are paid to the original payment method within 10 business days after the returned unit passes inspection at the warehouse.

chunks.title: Shipping and delivery times
chunks.text:
In stock: shipped the next business day if the order is confirmed before 14:00, delivered in 1-2 business days within the region.

In transit: the ETA is shown in the CRM on the model card and is usually 5-12 business days. Do not quote a date that is earlier than the ETA in the CRM.

On order: 4-6 weeks from the moment the prepayment is received. Custom voltages and coatings add 2 weeks.

Delivery is free for orders above $1,500 before tax; below that the courier rate from the price list applies. Pallet deliveries to construction sites need a contact person and a crane or forklift on site, which the customer confirms in writing.

chunks.title: Spare parts and lead times
chunks.text:
Motors, impellers and capacitors for current models are stocked for 7 years after the model is discontinued.

Spare parts in stock ship in 1-2 days. Parts that are not in stock take 3-5 weeks. Spare parts are not discounted.

chunks.title: Stock reservations
chunks.text:
A reservation holds stock items for a customer for 3 business days. Open the model card, press "Reserve", choose the customer and the quantity.

Only confirmed orders hold stock longer. When a reservation expires, the items return to free stock automatically and the manager gets a notification.

In-transit items can be reserved too; the reservation then starts on the day the shipment arrives.

chunks.title: Vacation and day-off requests
chunks.text:
Request vacation at least 2 weeks ahead: in the CRM go to Profile → Requests → New request, choose the type and the dates. Your manager approves it.

Sick leave: tell your manager by phone in the morning and create the request on the day you are back, with the certificate attached.

chunks.title: How to register a warranty claim (RMA) in the CRM
chunks.text: 1. Open the customer card and go to the "Claims" tab, then press "New claim". 2. Choose the order the unit came from. The serial number field is mandatory; the CRM checks that the serial belongs to that order. 3. Attach photos of the nameplate and of the fault, and the customer's description in their own words. 4. Pick the claim type: "Does not start", "Noise or vibration", "Low airflow", "Damaged on delivery" or "Other". 5. Save. The claim gets a number like RMA-2026-0153 and is routed to the service engineer on duty.

chunks.title: Can a customer return a made-to-order fan?
chunks.text: No. Units that were made to order (status "on order" at the time of sale, custom voltage or coating) cannot be returned. The 24-month warranty still applies to them.

chunks.title: Who approves a 10% discount?
chunks.text: The head of sales. Discounts from 5% to 12% need her approval: press "Request discount" on the quote and give the reason. Up to 5% a manager decides alone; above 12% only the sales director, and only for project deals.

chunks.title: Are spare parts discounted?
chunks.text: No. Spare parts and commissioning services are never discounted.

chunks.title: What is the most common reason for a low airflow claim?
chunks.text: A clogged filter or a wrong duty point. Ask for the filter's last replacement date and the duct layout before promising a replacement.
